- When sentiment is consistently negative (0.00) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.00), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% in those periods.
- If sentiment is positive (1.00) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to counteract downward drift.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) and recent price is trending down; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); reduce first 3–5 days by 0.5–1.5% to align with observed decay.
- When sentiment is positive and price is near support, model tends to ignore support levels; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to prevent overbought overcorrection.
